cohort: 72 pregnant women receiving prenatal care at Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujib Medical University Gynaecology and Obstetrics Division between December 2018 and March 2019.
finding: Among the 72 pregnant women, 34.7% had pre-eclampsia, 37.1% had pregnancy-induced hypertension, and 27.8% had eclampsia, with eclampsia being associated with low birth weight, pre-term delivery, and prenatal mortality.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rate was 51% overall, and was higher among women with pregnancy-induced hypertension and pre-eclampsia.
gest_age: 27.8% of newborns were delivered before 37 weeks, while 72.2% were delivered at or after 37 weeks.
